text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Some vague accord has been reached by Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia and Boualem Benhamouda, leader of the National Liberation Front (FLN) party, and separately with Mahfoud Nahnah, chief of the Islamist-oriented Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS), on a government line-up. The accord gives the FLN the secretary of state for Maghreb Affairs portfolio on top of seven other cabinet portfolios. MPS gets six positions in the government composition. The MPS leadership has endorsed the accord but FLN leaders were keeping their decision until this morning. The government list will be announced on Tuesday if the FLN approves the proposals.

- The marriage between pro-government National Democratic Rally (RND), FLN and MPS has not been consummated. The FLN wants to forge an FLN-RND alliance before forming a three-party coalition government with MPS.
- An explosion occurred on Monday at Tazrout village in the northeastern Bejaia province but there were no casualties.
- President Liamine Zeroual meets farm union leaders and pledges the state's full support for the agricultural sector.
- Construction of a highway linking the eastern city of Constantine to the western town of Oran could create 50,000 jobs.
